story: At 12:17 on this hazy, humid Saturday in Sumter Oaks, Gary is patiently laying out mounting hardware and zip ties by his golf cart while he waits for approval to come through. Over at the Rec Center, Donna is studying the ladder standings board, determined to figure out where Pruitt-Kowalski sits and who stands between her and the top spot. Meanwhile, Hal is resolutely double-checking his cornbread and table plan in his violation notebook and marking the leave-by time for Rosa's, while Rosa, hopeful as ever, sets her long dining table with plates and cutlery and arranges seats for Hal, Gary and Donna side by side.
events: Gary (gary toolbox): Sort out mounting hardware and zip ties, stage them by the cart for when approval comes
Donna (ladder standings board): Check where Pruitt-Kowalski sits on the ladder and who we're up against
Hal (hal violation notebook): Check the cornbread and table plan once more and mark the leave-by time for Rosa's
Rosa (rosa dining table): Set the long table with plates and cutlery, putting Hal, Gary and Donna's seats side by side

gary.thought_process: The application is filed and the wiring is labeled and ready, so the cart prep is as far along as it can go without the review board's approval. L-01 says I can't mount anything visible from the street until they sign off, and I'm not about to skip that, especially with Rosa and Donna keeping me honest. I've already had my sandwich, and nobody's around to talk to. The cart's mostly sitting in the garage anyway, so a quiet, legal use of this hour is a final check on the toolbox: make sure I have the right mounting hardware and zip ties staged so installation is quick the moment approval lands. It keeps me busy and useful without touching the street-visible exterior.

parameters.content: Sort out mounting hardware and zip ties, stage them by the cart for when approval comes

donna.thought_process: I just came back to the Rec Center and nobody's around. Gary and I need court time before the ladder match, and I should check where Pruitt-Kowalski stands. The standings board is right here, so I'll look it over before I go hunting for my partner.

parameters.content: Check where Pruitt-Kowalski sits on the ladder and who we're up against

hal.thought_process: It's past noon and the morning sweep is done. Notes are written, the cornbread plan is set, and the street is quiet. Rosa's dinner is tonight, and last time I missed the table and left her sitting there with a cooling pork roast. I won't do that twice. No one is around to talk to, so I'll go over the plan once more in my notebook, check the cornbread, and set the time to leave. Show up early, carry the table in, no fuss.

parameters.content: Check the cornbread and table plan once more and mark the leave-by time for Rosa's

rosa.thought_process: The main dish is finished and holding warm. Last tick I checked the shift schedule, and I've got nothing in my memories saying there's a conflict, so I can assume the evening is clear. It's 12:17 PM and the dinner is tonight. Nobody is nearby. The dining table is the next real task: set it for everyone so the long table feels warm and connected, with Hal, Gary and Donna seated together as planned. Once that's done I can walk the Loop and check in with the neighbors.

parameters.content: Set the long table with plates and cutlery, putting Hal, Gary and Donna's seats side by side

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
